lines.trans: Guys, tell us, how is your Eagle doing?
Oh, you have an eagle too, in childhood I had a parrot.
Vitya, Eagle is a horse, he is their main champion.
Unfortunately, it was such a big loss.
Let us not talk about sad things, your Eagle has long been in heaven.

examples.text: Ничего не хочу слышать, снова наливай!
examples.trans: I do not want to hear anything, pour again!

examples.text: Максим, ты снова возвращаешься на кухню.
examples.trans: Maxim, you are returning to the kitchen again.

examples.text: Я теперь снова здесь повар.
examples.trans: Now I am a cook here again.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'лноваться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'worry'.

examples.text: Не волнуйся.
examples.trans: Don't worry.

examples.text: Я волнуюсь.
examples.trans: I'm nervous.

examples.text: Не волнуйся, не буду.
examples.trans: Don't worry, I won't.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'knew'.

examples.text: Ну, раз целовались, значит, мы встречаемся.
examples.trans: Well, since we kissed, that means we are dating.

examples.text: Подожди, значит, я теперь уборщик?
examples.trans: Wait, so I am a cleaner now?

examples.text: Пожалуйста, знакомьтесь, это мой Виктор Петрович.
examples.trans: Please get acquainted, this is my Viktor Petrovich.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я надеюсь, что у нас есть целая жизнь.
examples.trans: I hope that we have a whole life.

examples.text: Сказал, что его блюда едят только в ресторане.
examples.trans: He said that his dishes are eaten only in the restaurant.

examples.text: Потому что я его с кухни выгнал.
examples.trans: Because I kicked him out of the kitchen.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'чить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to teach', paired with 'выучить'.

examples.text: Витя, скажи, что у тебя случилось?
examples.trans: Vitya, tell me, what happened with you?

examples.text: Вы не волнуйтесь, я знал, что буду учить новичков, и подготовился.
examples.trans: Do not worry, I knew I would be teaching beginners and prepared.

examples.text: Ну давай выпьем за то, чтобы у нас всё получилось.
examples.trans: Well let us drink to everything working out for us.

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'beginners' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Но вы новички, мы сыграем короткий вариант, часа через два закончим.
examples.trans: But you are beginners, we will play a short version and finish in two hours.

examples.text: Вы не волнуйтесь, я знал, что буду учить новичков, и подготовился.
examples.trans: Do not worry, I knew I would be teaching beginners and prepared.

examples.text: Всем новичкам всегда везёт.
examples.trans: All beginners always get lucky.

meanings.en: to prepare, to get oneself ready
meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'готовиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'prepared', paired with 'готовиться'.

examples.text: Подготовиться и поехать на дебаты.
examples.trans: Get ready and go to the debate.

examples.text: Успокоить жену! Подготовиться и поехать на дебаты.
examples.trans: Calm your wife down! Get ready and go to the debate.

examples.text: Мне нужно срочно подготовиться к встрече.
examples.trans: I need to prepare for the meeting urgently.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on, well', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Дмитрий Владимирович, у вас есть минутка?
examples.trans: Dmitry Vladimirovich, do you have a minute?

examples.text: Вчера, когда ты в кино крепко уснула.
examples.trans: Yesterday, when you fell fast asleep at the movies.

examples.text: Ну, раз целовались, значит, мы встречаемся.
examples.trans: Well, since we kissed, that means we are dating.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

related.gloss: to give (the verb it comes from)

examples.text: Давай выпьем хорошего шампанского.
examples.trans: Let us drink some good champagne.

examples.text: Наши выиграли, давай скорее наливай!
examples.trans: Our team won, come on, pour quickly!

examples.text: Конечно, можешь, только давай быстро.
examples.trans: Of course you may, just make it quick.

meanings.en: to drink up, to have a drink
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'пить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'let's drink', paired with 'выпивать'.

examples.text: Ой, сейчас что-то я выпила.
examples.trans: Oh, I've had a bit to drink now.

examples.text: Выпей воды.
examples.trans: Drink some water.

examples.text: Можно я выпью капельку пива?
examples.trans: May I drink a tiny drop of beer?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Сказал, что его блюда едят только в ресторане.
examples.trans: He said that his dishes are eaten only in the restaurant.

examples.text: Мы же с тобой в кино ходили три раза.
examples.trans: After all, you and I went to the movies three times.

examples.text: А я часа через два к тебе заеду.
examples.trans: And I will drop by your place in about two hours.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я надеюсь, что у нас есть целая жизнь.
examples.trans: I hope that we have a whole life.

examples.text: Сказал, что его блюда едят только в ресторане.
examples.trans: He said that his dishes are eaten only in the restaurant.

examples.text: Я тоже не понимаю, встречаемся мы или нет.
examples.trans: I also do not understand whether we are dating or not.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'so that, in order to', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я надеюсь, что у нас есть целая жизнь.
examples.trans: I hope that we have a whole life.

examples.text: Сказал, что его блюда едят только в ресторане.
examples.trans: He said that his dishes are eaten only in the restaurant.

examples.text: Потому что я его с кухни выгнал.
examples.trans: Because I kicked him out of the kitchen.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'us', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я тоже не понимаю, встречаемся мы или нет.
examples.trans: I also do not understand whether we are dating or not.

examples.text: Мы же с тобой в кино ходили три раза.
examples.trans: After all, you and I went to the movies three times.

examples.text: И мы там с тобой даже целовались.
examples.trans: And you and I even kissed there.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Всё, договорились, твоё условие принято.
examples.trans: That is it, we agreed, your condition is accepted.

examples.text: Всё, мы с тобой договорились.
examples.trans: That is it, you and I have a deal.

examples.text: Будешь курьером по доставке еды, всё, разговор окончен.
examples.trans: You will be a food delivery courier, that is all, the conversation is over.

meanings.en: to turn out, to work out
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лучиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'turned out', paired with 'получаться'.

examples.text: Всё получится!
examples.trans: It will all work out!

examples.text: Из него получится хороший врач.
examples.trans: He'll make a good doctor.

examples.text: Классный из тебя мэр получится, Самсон.
examples.trans: You'll make a great mayor, Samson.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'it seems', paired with 'показаться'.

examples.text: Алло, можно заказать билет на поезд до Воронежа?
examples.trans: Hello, may I book a train ticket to Voronezh?

examples.text: Мне кажется, он прав.
examples.trans: I think he's right.

examples.text: Я вас видел, кажется.
examples.trans: I think I've seen you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: И мы там с тобой даже целовались.
examples.trans: And you and I even kissed there.

examples.text: К счастью, там, куда мы едем, костюм тебе не понадобится.
examples.trans: Fortunately, where we are going, you will not need a suit.

examples.text: Что у вас там, слоны?
examples.trans: What do you have there, elephants?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'someone', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ой, кажется, там к нам кто-то пришёл.
examples.trans: Oh, it seems someone has come to our door.

examples.text: Наконец-то кто-то за народ!
examples.trans: Finally someone is for the people!

examples.text: Слушай, тут пишут: «Гордость России! Наконец-то кто-то за народ!»
examples.trans: Listen, here they write: 'Pride of Russia! Finally someone is for the people!'

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'arrived', paired with 'приходить'.

examples.text: Сейчас придёт охрана.
examples.trans: Security will be here any moment.

examples.text: Я приду завтра.
examples.trans: I'll come tomorrow.

examples.text: Не надо, Самсон. Сейчас придёт охрана.
examples.trans: Don't, Samson. Security will be here any second.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'верное').

examples.text: Наверное, обед привезли наш, я пойду открою.
examples.trans: They probably brought our lunch, I will go open the door.

examples.text: Ладно, я, наверное, сейчас домой поеду.
examples.trans: Alright, I will probably drive home right now.

examples.text: Ну, наверное, в архиве где-то.
examples.trans: Well, probably somewhere in the archive.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'lunch' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Наверное, обед привезли наш, я пойду открою.
examples.trans: They probably brought our lunch, I will go open the door.

examples.text: У нашей команды появился шанс вырвать победу!
examples.trans: Our team has a chance to snatch victory!

examples.text: У меня перерыв на обед.
examples.trans: I have my lunch break.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'везти'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'delivered / brought', paired with 'привозить'.

examples.text: Наверное, обед привезли наш, я пойду открою.
examples.trans: They probably brought our lunch, I will go open the door.

examples.text: Я Максим, а вы мне билет привезли?
examples.trans: I am Maxim, and did you bring me the ticket?

examples.text: Папа привёз подарки.
examples.trans: Dad brought presents.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'our', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Наш шеф уволил курьера по доставке еды.
examples.trans: Our chef fired the food delivery courier.

examples.text: Меня наш шеф обратно не возьмёт.
examples.trans: Our chef will not take me back.

examples.text: Сегодня наш любимый клуб «Спартак» играет.
examples.trans: Today our favorite club Spartak is playing.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will go', paired with 'идти'.

examples.text: Извините, я пойду работать.
examples.trans: Excuse me, I will go work.

examples.text: Наверное, обед привезли наш, я пойду открою.
examples.trans: They probably brought our lunch, I will go open the door.

examples.text: Я сейчас пойду открою.
examples.trans: I will go open the door right now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'крыть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will open', paired with 'открывать'.

examples.text: Откройте дверь.
examples.trans: Open the door.

examples.text: Открой окно.
examples.trans: Open the window.

examples.text: Откройте дверь. Квартира девять?
examples.trans: Open the door. Is this flat nine?
